patch_apply_checks: git apply --reverse --check in the fix tree
qemu.parallel_layers: 0117-atomecho-board and 0119-unit-i2c-batch2 are unrelated parallel layers merged separately; git apply --check of 0118 was verified on 0116, 0116+0117, 0116+0119 and 0116+0117+0119.

root_cause.problem: GC0308 DVP output geometry was fixed at the board-attached QVGA 320x240, so any other framesize requested through camera.init(framesize=...) produced a frame byte length that did not match the LCD_CAM/DMA frame the driver assembled (QQVGA returned 38400 bytes of a QVGA stream, CIF/VGA returned no complete frame).
root_cause.guest_path: esp32-camera set_framesize() (sensors/gc0308.c, CONFIG_GC_SENSOR_SUBSAMPLE_MODE) writes GC0308 page 0 0x09/0x0a (window height + 8) and 0x0b/0x0c (window width + 8), then page 1 0x54/0x56-0x59 (subsample ratio). Output resolution = window * ratio.

fix: m5sw_i2c_devs.c: the GC0308 model decodes the window/subsample register pair with an exact integer inverse for the eight esp32-camera subsample configurations and publishes the output geometry to the bound LCD_CAM device.

m5_lcd_cam.c: stores the sensor geometry and latches it at CAM_START, so partially written register sets cannot change a running frame; the synthetic scene advances one white-grid row per frame (frame_seed 0 keeps the original pattern) so consecutive streamed frames stay distinct.
m5atoms3rcam.c: binds the board GC0308 model to the LCD_CAM instance.

geometry_cases.name: QVGA
geometry_cases.note: module default framesize; keeps the original single-frame oracle

stream.oracle: each guest digest equals the sha256 of a host-reconstructed QVGA frame for a distinct frame_seed; no frame matched a torn/partial buffer
stream.enable_path: QOM /machine/m5-lcd-cam auto-increment=true is applied by the console matrix runner when the guest prints CAM_BASE_DONE, i.e. after the static-frame oracle and before the stream captures (no host frame data is injected)

regression.cores3-camera: PASS (peripheral matrix: CORES3_CAMERA_PASS 320x240 153600 bytes, CORES3_CAMERA_FRAMESTREAM PASS 1)

not_run: physical optics, exposure/white balance, sensor noise and electrical DVP/SCCB timing or drive strength
dynamic framesize change while frames are streaming (the probe re-initializes the camera per size; LCD_CAM latches geometry at CAM_START)
frame sizes above VGA (the GC0308 driver clamps to VGA) and non-4:3 sizes not in the esp32-camera resolution table
IR GPIO47, Grove G2/G1 Units, USB CDC console and arbitrary third-party firmware
the modeled scene is a deterministic synthetic DVP waveform, not captured optics
